thread:
maria: Quick check — onboarding falcon-x-50b weights to hosted pool. We pushed weights to gs://redwood-models/releases/falcon-x/2026-03-17 but the tokenizer seems to insert an extra leading token in our chat templates. Seeing chat-format test failures. Anyone seen this before?
sam: I ran into something similar last month. Falcon variant uses  sentinel and also a <|chat|> token. Usually it's a tokenizer preset mismatch. Which tokenizers.json are you using?
maria: Using tokenizers/falconx-bpe-v2.json from the repo. Example prompt: "User: Hi
Assistant:" encodes with an extra token before the expected BOS. Failing chat-format tests.
lee: @maria can you paste a tiny encode output (raw ids)? Quick run: `python -c "from tokenizer import Encoder; print(Encoder.encode('User: Hi\nAssistant:'))"` — that'll help isolate.
maria: Encode output (sanitized): tokens  -> 5 203 12 1024 ... so the first token is 5 which I don't expect as BOS in our model_config.
sam: 5 is the  token in the v1 tokenizer mapping. Looks like model_config.json lists "bos_token_id": 0 while the tokenizer maps BOS to 5. That's the mismatch.
maria: Oh — weights were exported with bos=5. I'll try changing model_config to bos_token_id: 5 and re-run tests. Any downstream effects on promptwrap?
sam: Prompt templates assume we strip the leading BOS when concatenating messages. If we update model_config, we should also ensure promptwrap strips tokens[0] when it's the BOS sentinel. Quick patch: in prompt_wrap.py add `if tokens and tokens[0] == model_config['bos_token_id']: tokens = tokens[1:]` before caching.
maria: Good call. I'll add that to the PR. Also noticed the loader picked the v1 checkpoint by default — weights path matters.
lee: Important: the bucket has both v1 and v2. The loader defaults to /checkpoint if you don't point to /v2/checkpoint-0002. @maria confirm which path you're using.
maria: I pointed to gs://redwood-models/releases/falcon-x/2026-03-17 (no subpath). Switched to /v2/checkpoint-0002 now and re-ran smoke. Chat-format tests mostly pass, except emoji handling — some emoji split into extra tokens and that throws off prefix counts.
sam: Emoji splitting is usually normalization. We currently use NFD normalization in the tokenizer pipeline; switching to NFKC reduces grapheme splitting for many emoji sequences. I'll open a follow-up to change normalization strategy and add a targeted test.
lee: For immediate fix, consider adding a small postprocess step in prompt formatting that merges leading zero-width joiner sequences or collapses emoji sequences into single tokens if tokenizer reports multiple. That avoids cache misalignment until we roll the tokenizer change.
maria: Opening PR now: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/789 — updates model_config bos id, promptwrap strip, and weights path to /v2/checkpoint-0002. @sam please review normalization follow-up.
sam: Quick review done. Left two tiny style comments. Also: add a line in release manifest that pins tokenizer version used to produce weights (helps future onboarding).
lee: I'll run canary after merge. Dev canary checklist: verify token counts on sample prompts, run chat_integration with prefix cache enabled, confirm latency SLO unaffected. I'll post results.
dev-bot: CI queued for PR #789 — jobs: tokenizer_smoke, chat_integration, release_manifest_check.
maria: Action items summarized: (1) Sam: open normalization ticket + test (2) Maria: update release manifest and merge PR after CI green (3) Lee: run canary and report. I'll hold merge until CI passes and canary looks good. :thumbsup:
lee: Sounds good — pinging #eng-ml once canary is green. :eyes:
